mealPlan.name: Lemon Herb Baked Salmon with Roasted Asparagus and Quinoa
mealPlan.instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). In a small saucepan, combine 1/4 cup dry quinoa with 1/2 cup water or vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Set aside.
2. Wash asparagus and trim the tough ends. Toss with 1/2 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
3. Pat salmon fillet dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix the remaining 1/2 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, chopped dill, chopped parsley, lemon juice (from 1/4 lemon), salt, and pepper. Spread this mixture evenly over the top of the salmon fillet.
4. Place the salmon fillet on the same baking sheet as the asparagus (or a separate small one). Roast in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, and asparagus is tender-crisp.
5. Serve the baked salmon and roasted asparagus immediately alongside the cooked quinoa. Garnish with fresh lemon slices (from the remaining 1/4 lemon) if desired.
mealPlan.tips: For an extra flavor boost, try adding a sprinkle of chili flakes to the salmon before baking if you tolerate a mild warmth, or use smoked paprika for a non-spicy alternative. Leftover quinoa can be stored in the fridge for up to 3-4 days and used in salads or as a side dish. Ensure your salmon is completely thawed if using frozen.

ingredientItems.notes: skin on or off, your preference
